# A. Path Affine Composition

Store every HLD interval in a segment tree with forward and backward affine
composition. Merging adjacent intervals composes left-forward then
right-forward; backward uses right-backward then left-backward. Split a path
into upward `u` chunks, a same-chain middle, and downward `v` chunks, preserving
their order.

**Correctness.** Segment induction proves both stored directions. Each HLD
chunk is a contiguous part of the path. The accumulation rules concatenate
these disjoint chunks in exact `u -> v` order, so the final affine function is
precisely the sequence requested. Applying it to `x` gives the answer.

Preprocessing is `O(n)`. Updates cost `O(log n)` and queries `O(log^2 n)`;
memory is `O(n)`. Test reversed paths with functions that do not commute.

# B. Toggle Nearest Beacon

Build centroid decomposition and record every vertex's distance to each
centroid ancestor. Each centroid owns a multiset of distances contributed by
active vertices. Toggle inserts or erases one distance along the vertex's
centroid path. Query minimizes its own distance to `c` plus the multiset minimum
at `c`.

**Correctness.** For any query vertex `u` and active vertex `v`, their centroid
paths share the first separator at which their original-tree path crosses
between decomposition components; at that centroid `c`,
`dist(u,v)=dist(u,c)+dist(v,c)`. The candidate is therefore present. Every
candidate is the length of a concrete route through its centroid and cannot be
smaller than the true distance. Taking the minimum is exact.

Build time is `O(n log n)`. Toggle and query cost `O(log^2 n)` with multisets;
memory is `O(n log n)`. Python uses paired lazy-deletion heaps.

{{< include problems/b_toggle_nearest_beacon/solution.cpp >}}

# C. Marked Pair Distances

Sort marked vertices by Euler time, add LCAs of consecutive entries, sort and
deduplicate, then connect them by an ancestor stack. Initialize each marked
virtual vertex with count one. Process virtual vertices bottom-up. For edge
`p-u`, add

```text
(dist[u]-dist[p]) * count[u] * (k-count[u]).
```

and transfer `count[u]` to `p`.

**Correctness.** The virtual tree preserves every branching LCA and compresses
only degree-two unmarked paths, so its edge length equals the removed original
path. Removing edge `p-u` separates `count[u]` marks from the other
`k-count[u]`; exactly their cross pairs use every original edge represented by
it. Summing over virtual edges counts each pair once per edge on its path,
which is exactly its distance.

Preprocessing costs `O(n log n)`. A query costs `O(k log k)` and uses `O(k)`
temporary memory. Test one mark, ancestor relations, and LCAs absent from the
input set.

# D. Subtree Mode Sum

Process vertices bottom-up. Reuse the largest child frequency map, merge every
smaller child map into it, then add the current color. Maintain the maximum
frequency and sum of colors attaining it whenever a count increases.

**Correctness.** By induction, child maps contain exactly their disjoint
subtrees. Their union plus the current vertex is exactly the current subtree,
independent of merge order. The maintained maximum resets its sum when a
strictly larger count appears and adds a color when it ties, so the reported
sum is exact.

Every color entry moves only into a map at least twice as large, at most
`O(log n)` times. Expected time is `O(n log n)` and memory `O(n)`. Test ties,
all equal colors, all distinct colors, chains, and stars.

# Stress testing and carry-forward

The generators use explicit path reconstruction, all-pairs tree distances, and
complete subtree color counters. The recurring discovery move is to choose the
small boundary: logarithmically many chains/centroids, `O(k)` virtual vertices,
or entries that can move only logarithmically often.
